l2.name: Social Disadvantage
l2.description: Personal experiences of discrimination — bias in contracting, exclusion from networks, personal prejudice

l2.name: Economic Disadvantage
l2.description: Capital access barriers — denied loans, bonding difficulties, financial limitations

l2.name: Institutional/Systemic Barrier
l2.description: Discriminatory institutional policies — not individual acts, but systemic patterns

l2.name: Ordinary Business Risk
l2.description: Setbacks from normal market forces — competition, pricing, general economy

l2.name: Insufficient Evidence
l2.description: The incident lacks enough detail to classify under §26.67

l3.name: Meets Requirements of SED (No Race or Sex Presumptions)
l3.title: Meets Requirements of SED
l3.pass: Narrative includes individualized examples of social and economic disadvantage and is not based in whole or in part on race or sex.
l3.fail: Narrative does not include individualized examples of social and economic disadvantage or relies on race or sex presumptions.

l3.name: Meets Personal Net Worth (PNW < $2.047M)
l3.title: Meets Personal Net Worth (PNW)
l3.rule: Review the Excel Cross-Reference Revenue/PNW. HOWEVER, if the 'Narrative Declared PNW' provides a specific number, it OVERRIDES the Excel data.

l3.name: Meets Disadvantage in American Society
l3.title: Meets Disadvantage in American Society
l3.pass: Narrative provides experience of social and economic disadvantage within American society.
l3.fail: Narrative does not describe experiences of social and economic disadvantage within American society.

l3.name: Demonstration of Disadvantage (Past Experiences)
l3.pass: Narrative provides clear, specific individualized examples of lived experiences of social and economic disadvantage within American society that impeded progress or success.
l3.fail: Narrative provides only general statements of social and economic disadvantage without clear, specific, and individualized examples.

l3.name: Evidence of Specific Impediments
l3.pass: Narrative describes fact-based examples of systemic barriers, denied opportunities, and/or economic hardship (e.g. education, employment, business, financing) that establishes the existence of disadvantage by a preponderance of the evidence (i.e., is more probable than not).
l3.fail: Narrative mentions barriers in broad/general terms without supporting detail or provides no examples of specific impediments that establishes the existence of disadvantage by a preponderance of the evidence.

l3.name: Link Between Impediments and Harm
l3.pass: Narrative clearly explains how impediments or barriers caused direct economic harm; includes detail on the type and magnitude (e.g., lost contracts, financial losses, comparative disadvantage).
l3.fail: Narrative states economic harm occurred but does not explain how the barriers caused economic harm.

l3.name: Economic Disadvantage in Fact
l3.pass: Narrative and financial data demonstrates that the owner is economically disadvantaged compared to similarly situated non-disadvantaged individuals.
l3.fail: Narrative mentions economic disadvantage but provides weak, inconsistent, or no evidence of such disadvantage.

l3_custom.name: Specific Quantified Economic Harm
l3_custom.pass:
Narrative quantifies at least one economic harm with concrete figures — e.g., a
  specific dollar amount lost, a named contract or bid, a percentage revenue decline, the
   number of jobs missed, or any other numeric or named-event evidence of magnitude
l3_custom.fail:
Narrative describes economic harm only in qualitative or generalized terms (e.g.,
  "missed opportunities", "lost contracts", "difficulty obtaining loans") without dollar
  amounts, named contracts, dates, or any other quantified or specifically-identified
  loss.
